text: For the zinc, I'd use zinc carnosine, since it's better tolerated than other forms of zinc and also helps repair leaky gut (Mahmood, et al, 2007). A standard dose is up to 75 mg a day, which holds 16 mg of elemental zinc, and if it causes nausea, take less at a time. Zinc can lower your copper over time, so I'd also take 1–2 mg of elemental copper a day, as copper gluconate or citrate (not cupric oxide, which is poorly absorbed). For L-serine, I'd do 5–15 g a day, depending how it feels. Higher doses bring more GI distress, though up to 30 g a day has been used in trials for neurodegenerative conditions (Levine, et al, 2017).

checked.point: zinc carnosine helps repair leaky gut
checked.found: Mahmood 2007 (Gut): 37.5 mg twice daily kept healthy volunteers' gut permeability from rising on indomethacin; Davison 2016 (AJCN): it cut the rise in gut permeability after heavy exercise by 70%
checked.still_needed: yes: they pick zinc carnosine over a cheaper zinc, knowing what it does for their gut too (his reason, his answer 58)

checked.point: L-serine up to 30 g a day in trials for neurodegenerative conditions, more stomach trouble higher
checked.found: Levine 2017 (phase I trial in ALS): up to 15 g twice daily, generally well tolerated, two of 20 left with stomach problems
checked.still_needed: yes: they keep to 5-15 g and don't chase higher doses, knowing trials went to 30 g and the stomach suffers above the range (his point, his answer 58)
